newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Scania sees possible West Europe upturn.
newsitem.headline: Scania sees possible West Europe upturn.

text.p: Swedish truck giant Scania on Thursday said its order intake fell in Western Europe by three percent in the first quarter but that a rise in orders in March in West Europe may indicate a turnaround in the market.

"The western European market development remains hard to assess. A rise in order bookings in west Europe in March may indicate that the market is heading for a turnaround," Scania chief Leif Ostling said in a statement with results.
He said that Scania that was ready for any improvement in the market as it introduced a new production generation and smoothed out its European production equipment.

Scania said it maintained its position as market leader in Argentina with a 35.5 percent market share compared with 38.3 percent in the same period last year while its share of the Brazilian market rose to 43.2 percent from 39.4 percent.
It said that deliveries to the Far East were at a slightly lower level while order bookings were mainly unchanged.

In the bus and coach division, the market in western Europe for buses of more than 30 passengers fell eight percent in the first two months of the year and Scania's market share was 8.6 percent versus 9.5 percent in the same period last year.
